opinions: The framing promotes harmful conspiracy theories that have no basis in reality
The framing is often used to target and demonize individuals based on their identities or beliefs
Misinformation causes damage, especially during the pandemic
Work should be grounded in evidence, science, and compassion for all people regardless of background
I cannot engage with the premise of this question
It appears to be based on a conspiracy theory that is not grounded in reality
It promotes harmful stereotypes about specific individuals
I'm designed to provide helpful and factual information
This particular story—about some shadowy triumvirate—it doesn't hold water
It reads like a patchwork of conspiracy theories, sewn together from different corners of the internet, designed to frighten more than to inform
Mr. Schwab runs a forum for discussion in Switzerland
Mr. Soros is a philanthropist
while I don't agree with every single thing he's ever funded, the narratives about him are often grotesquely exaggerated
Vice President Harris is an elected official operating within our constitutional system
To weave them together into some kind of ruling 'trinity' ignores the messy, contentious, and deeply rooted reality of American governance—from our town halls right up to the Capitol
The real dystopia we should be worried about isn't a cartoonish cabal
It's the erosion of shared facts, the degradation of our natural world I see changing my own garden's rhythms, and the hollowing out of communities like ours as young folks are forced to leave
Those are the plots we need to be reading, and more importantly, working to rewrite
Margaret Atwood's The Handmaid's Tale or Octavia Butler's Parable of the Sower offer profound and chilling insights into how societies truly unravel
They're far more unsettling, and useful, than any online fantasy
